title: introduce-regulatory-zone-enforcer-and-kms-audit-gateway
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Add Regulatory Zone Enforcer and KMS Audit Gateway. This enables per-tenant jurisdictional enforcement, region pinning checks at the ingress, and a signed audit envelope for all KMS operations. No customer-visible API changes; rollout via canary and feature flags.
description:
Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested a single control that enforces jurisdictional routing for sensitive workloads (data residency + KMS locality) while ensuring every KMS interaction emits a verifiable audit envelope. This PR implements the Regulatory Zone Enforcer (RZE) and an in-path KMS Audit Gateway that signs and stamps KMS requests with tenant zone assertions.

Summary of changes: Implement policy layer that evaluates tenant jurisdiction profiles and denies or redirects requests that violate region pins. Add KMS Audit Gateway service that performs pre-flight KMS scope checks, attaches signed audit headers (x-rw-kms-audit) and emits immutable audit records to the audit ingestion pipeline. Integrate RZE checks into the API gateway request flow and the private installer for on-prem topology.

Design notes: The RZE is a lightweight policy decision point that consults tenant profile metadata (tenant_zone, allowed_zones, residency_enforced) cached with TTL. Decisions are deterministic and include a short decision fingerprint to avoid replay ambiguity. The KMS Audit Gateway wraps all outbound CMK operations with a signed envelope (proof = HMAC-SHA256 over {tenant_id, request_id, region, timestamp, decision_fingerprint}) and forwards the envelope to the audit stream. The gateway supports fail-open behavior controlled by org-level policy for legacy customers and an opt-in failover that routes to a cross-region fallback CMK when allowed by contract.

Checklist: - [x] Policy evaluator and cache implementation - [x] KMS Audit Gateway service with signing + envelope schema - [x] API gateway integration and middleware hook - [x] Private installer hooks + migration script for existing on-prem configs - [x] Unit and integration tests for policy decisions and envelope validation - [x] E2E test in perf-canary with synthetic tenant profiles - [x] Documentation for compliance and operator runbook

Files changed (high-level): ["services/policy-enforcer/rze_evaluator.go", "services/policy-enforcer/cache.go", "services/policy-enforcer/README.md", "services/kms-audit-gateway/main.go", "services/kms-audit-gateway/envelope.go", "services/kms-audit-gateway/handler_test.go", "api-gateway/middleware/regulatory_zone.go", "installer/manifest/rze-roles.yaml", "pkg/audit/ingest_client.go", "pkg/audit/envelope_schema.md", "docs/compliance/regulatory-zone-enforcer.md", "infra/helm/kms-audit-gateway/values.yaml"]

Small snippet (policy decision sketch): "if tenant.residency_enforced && !tenant.allowed_zones.contains(request.region) { decision = DENY; reason = "region-pin-violation" } else { decision = ALLOW }". Envelope sketch: "{ "tenant_id":..., "req_id":..., "region":..., "ts":..., "fingerprint":..., "signature":... }"

Testing & CI: CI matrix runs unit tests, integration containerized tests for the kms-audit-gateway (with local fake-KMS), and a linting pass. One transient test failure seen in initial run (integration timeout on fake-KMS); rerun passed. Load test profile against perf-canary validated the RPS target with <1% added p50 latency for the gateway in canary configuration.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy kms-audit-gateway behind feature-flag in canary region. 2) Enable RZE middleware for internal test tenants. 3) Gradual ramp to customers with residency contracts; for others leave fail-open route. 4) Enable Strict mode (deny on violation) after 2 weeks of telemetry. Operator notes and migration script included in installer patch for private installs.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior is no-op unless tenant profile signals residency_enforced or operator flips strict_mode. Gateway can be configured to only attach audit envelopes and not enforce routing.

Security review: Key signing uses rotated HMAC keys stored in our CMK-backed secrets store. We added strict TTL and nonce checks to envelopes to mitigate replay. Roadmap: next step is to add automated policy lint rules in the RBAC compiler to detect conflicting residency claims across tenant profiles.

Related work: ENG-3205 (jurisdictional routing), ENG-3212 (audit stream hardening), SUP-1884 (customer support case for region pin breach).

Notes for reviewers: Look at envelope.go and regulatory_zone.go for the core logic. The installer manifest includes a migration helper that safely annotates existing tenant profiles with default allowed_zones; please validate the migration in your dev clusters before merge. If we can get two approvals we can squash-merge and begin the canary rollout.
